att_notes: IE-CoR (2023): present-day Magahi; Set on Patna, the capital of the Indian state of Bihar, the major town in which Magahi is spoken. (25.59, 85.14)
IE-CoR (2023): present-day Kashmiri; Set on Sharda (Neelum valley, Azad Jammu & Kashmir), the home of the main language consultant for these IE-CoR data. (34.793, 74.193)
IE-CoR (2023): present-day Hindi; Set on Delhi, India (28.704, 77.102)
IE-CoR (2023): present-day Nepali; Set at Kathmandu, the capital of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal and the major educational, cultural and literary centre for Nepali. (27.717, 85.323)

IE-CoR (2023): present-day Bhojpuri; Set on Gorakhpur, the town where the IE-CoR Bhojpuri data were elicited, and the centre of the Gorakhpuri dialect, one of the main dialects of Bhojpuri (26.76, 83.37)
IE-CoR (2023): present-day Bengali; Set on Kolkata (Calcutta), capital of the Indian state of West Bengal, and a cultural centre where Bengali is the dominant language. (22.57, 88.36)
IE-CoR (2023): present-day Urdu; Set on Islamabad, Pakistan (33.684, 73.047)
IE-CoR (2023): present-day Marathi; Set on Pune, India. (18.52, 73.856)
IE-CoR (2023): present-day Assamese; Set at Raha, Nagaon province, provenance of the informant from whom the data were elicited (26.23, 92.52)

IE-CoR (2023): present-day Maithili; Set on Madhubani, the cultural centre of the Mithila region, the home region of several renowned Maithili poets, among them Vidyapati Thakur, the ‘father of Mai (26.35, 86.08)
Pali canon: from c. 3rd c. BCE; written down in Sri Lanka, 1st c. BCE
